survivors.title: Core config loaders read glyph-bearing YAML with the platform-default encoding (cp1252 crash on Windows)
survivors.evidence: All four cached loaders call `read_text()` with NO encoding, e.g. line 292 `return _parse_yaml_records(paths.kinds_yaml().read_text())` (also 280 books, 316 categories, 341 editions). `Path.read_text()` defaults to `locale.getpreferredencoding()` = cp1252 on Windows. content/categories.yaml (and kinds.yaml) contain raw non-ASCII glyphs — confirmed: categories.yaml line 16 `symbol: "⌘"`, line 28 `symbol: "‖"`, etc. Decoding U+2318 (UTF-8 E2 8C 98) as cp1252 raises UnicodeDecodeError (byte 0x8C is undefined in cp1252). This is exactly the failure the project's own memory documents ('PYTHONUTF8 required — Windows runs need PYTHONUTF8=1 or 72 tests fail with cp1252 errors'); the only places PYTHONUTF8 is set are the test/CI runners (scripts/ci.py:69, scripts/pytest_gate_shard.py:64), NOT any app/CLI entrypoint (web.py/run.py/desktop_shell.py force no UTF-8 mode). So config.load_kinds()/load_categories() — the spine every consumer depends on — crash when run via plain `python`/`py -3` on Windows without the env var.
survivors.fix: Pass `encoding="utf-8"` explicitly to every loader read: `paths.kinds_yaml().read_text(encoding="utf-8")` (and the books/categories/editions reads). This removes the dependency on PYTHONUTF8 / platform locale and makes the loaders correct on every platform regardless of environment — the same fix already applied in notes_io.atomic_write (which passes encoding=).
survivors.verifierFix: Pass encoding="utf-8" to all four reads in scripts/core/config.py: line 280 paths.books_yaml().read_text(encoding="utf-8"); line 292 paths.kinds_yaml().read_text(encoding="utf-8"); line 316 p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") (categories); line 341 p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") (editions). This is additive and byte-neutral (identical to the current PYTHONUTF8/-X utf8 decode), so KJV byte-stability and the golden hashes are preserved. Two corrections to the finder's writeup: (a) the cited crash trigger is wrong — `⌘`/0x8C does NOT crash (0x8C is defined in cp1252); the actual UnicodeDecodeError comes from `❑` U+2751 / `❖` U+2756 in categories.yaml (lines 88/94), whose UTF-8 byte 0x9D is undefined in cp1252. (b) Do NOT remove the existing dev/launcher.spec `-X utf8` option or the CI PYTHONUTF8=1 — the spec comment shows the broader codebase (notes stores, HTML, Hebrew/Greek) still reads via unencoded read_text()/open(), so this 4-site fix only hardens the config spine; the scaffolding must stay until a full sweep is done.

survivors.title: _send_file magic-byte verification is defeated by the extension fallback in _detect_format — non-image bytes with a whitelisted extension are served with an image Content-Type
survivors.evidence: In _send_file the SEC-001 check does `ext = path.suffix.lower().lstrip(".")`, `ext_norm = "jpeg" if ext=="jpg" else ext`, then `fmt = _detect_format(data[:32], ext)`. But `_detect_format` (scripts/core/covers.py:269) returns `suffix.lstrip(".").lower()` when the magic bytes match NONE of png/jpeg/webp — i.e. it falls back to the extension passed in. So for a file `x.png` whose bytes are arbitrary (HTML, SVG, plain text, anything non-image), `fmt` becomes `"png"`, `ext_norm` is `"png"`, so BOTH guards pass: `fmt not in UPLOAD_ALLOWED_FORMATS` is False and the `if fmt != ext_norm:` ("Magic bytes disagree with extension — refuse to serve") never fires. The bytes are then served with `Content-Type: image/png`. The code comment claims 'a hostile file dropped under content/covers/ (via backup restore, scenario import, or hand placement) cannot be served as an image' and 'Magic bytes disagree with extension — refuse to serve' — neither guarantee holds for arbitrary content carrying a whitelisted extension. Note the UPLOAD validator does it correctly: validate_upload_image (covers.py:573) calls `_detect_format(data, "")` with an EMPTY fallback, forcing magic-byte-only detection; only the serve path (web.py:1347) passes the real extension and re-opens the hole. Real-world XSS impact is blocked by the response's `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` + `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox; img-src 'self'`, so this is a defense-in-depth/correctness gap rather than a live XSS, and reaching it requires local/back-channel file placement (uploads are validated). Checked all 3 _detect_format call sites: covers.py:573 (upload, safe — empty fallback), covers.py:369 (read_image_meta, informational only), web.py:1347 (serve, the affected site).
survivors.fix: In _send_file, detect format from magic bytes only by passing an empty fallback: `fmt = _detect_format(data[:32], "")` (mirroring validate_upload_image). Keep `if fmt not in UPLOAD_ALLOWED_FORMATS: return 415` so unrecognized content is refused regardless of filename, and keep the `if fmt != ext_norm: return 415` cross-check. This makes the serve-time guarantee actually match the comment and the upload validator, instead of relying solely on nosniff/CSP.

survivors.title: Flagship glossary from-file streamer's structural fallback re-materializes the whole-document str while still holding the 480 MB raw bytes (re-introduces the OOM the byte-streamer exists to prevent)
survivors.evidence:
_iter_study_glossary_pieces_from_file reads the ~480 MB monolith as bytes, then on a structural surprise falls back to the in-memory str splitter without freeing the bytes: `try:
    yield from _stream_glossary_pieces_from_bytes(raw, stem, target)
except _GlossaryStructureError:
    yield from _iter_study_glossary_pieces(_decode_nl(raw), stem, target)`. On the fallback, `raw` (~480 MB) is still bound in this frame while `_decode_nl(raw)` materializes the ~880 MB UCS-2 whole-document str (Hebrew/Greek/Ge'ez force 2-byte), which _iter_study_glossary_pieces then slices into head/body/inner before its own `del text` — peak ≈ raw(480MB)+str(880MB)+slices > 1.4 GB. That is exactly the MemoryError the _GLOSSARY_STREAM_BYTE_THRESHOLD byte-streamer was added to avoid (comment at 5245-5254). It is latent (only fires on _GlossaryStructureError, which the proven 690/690 real monolith does not hit), so it is not a re-raise of the shipped D5 streamer — it is the untested escape hatch that silently negates the fix on any future structural drift in the >64 MB glossary.
survivors.fix:
Free the byte buffer before decoding the fallback text so the two giant copies never co-reside: `except _GlossaryStructureError:
    text = _decode_nl(raw)
    raw = b""  # release the ~480 MB byte buffer before slicing
    yield from _iter_study_glossary_pieces(text, stem, target)`. Better still, stream the fallback from the file in bounded chunks rather than decoding the whole monolith, so the fallback path keeps the same RAM ceiling the byte-streamer guarantees. Add a regression that feeds a >64 MB structurally-irregular glossary through the from-file path and asserts peak RSS stays bounded.
survivors.verifierFix:
Free the 480 MB byte buffer BEFORE re-decoding the fallback text, so the old bytes never co-reside with the whole-document str during decode or streaming. Re-read from the already-available `path` (universal-newline read_text is content-identical to _decode_nl(read_bytes()): both translate CRLF/CR to LF and decode UTF-8), which lets the old raw be collected before the new decode allocates:

    try:
        yield from _stream_glossary_pieces_from_bytes(raw, stem, target)
    except _GlossaryStructureError:
        del raw  # release the ~480 MB byte buffer before the whole-document decode
        yield from _iter_study_glossary_pieces(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), stem, target)

survivors.evidence:
`_unescape` is `text.replace("<","<").replace(">",">").replace("&","&")` (lines 115-116) and the FAIL pattern `("py-repr-class", re.compile(r""))` (line 78) is applied ONLY to that partially-unescaped text. So an f-string/str() repr leak of a class — exactly the leak the dim targets — ships escaped and PASSES the headline gate. The `_selftest` only proves the RAW form (`"

raw ..."`, line 334), giving false confidence that the escaped form is covered.
survivors.fix: Replace the hand-rolled `_unescape` with the stdlib `import html; return html.unescape(text)` (decodes `'`, `"`, and numeric char refs as well as the three named entities), and add an html.escape'd repr (e.g. `html.escape("<class 'dict'>")`) to the `_selftest` `dirty` string so the escaped class-repr path is proven non-tautologically.

Confirmed: (a) _unescape (lines 115-116) decodes only </>/&, not '; (b) the FAIL pattern py-repr-class (line 78) is `<class '[\w.]+'>` requiring a literal apostrophe; (c) the gate deliberately scans an entity-unescaped copy (line 143 `unescaped = _unescape(stripped)` feeding _LEAK_FAIL_UNESCAPED at 149-152) specifically to catch escaped reprs (docstring lines 19-20 'Raw AND HTML-escaped forms are scanned'). Python's html.escape with quote=True maps '→', so a leaked <class 'dict'> escapes to <class 'dict'>, which _unescape turns into <class 'dict'> — the py-repr-class regex never matches it. Among the unescaped FAIL patterns, py-repr-class is the ONLY one containing apostrophes; object-at/callable/dict-view/traceback have none, so they survive _unescape and are fine. The _selftest (line 334) proves only the RAW <class 'dict'> form and (line 333) an escaped callable repr that has no apostrophes, so the escaped-class path is never exercised — confirming the false-confidence claim. It is not output corruption — it is a read-only audit false-negative — so I lower severity from medium to low (no shipped-output corruption, KJV editions stay byte-stable, no demonstrated live leak). The proposed fix (html.unescape + an html.escape'd class repr in the self-test) is correct and safe: stdlib, strictly more complete, only feeds the narrow repr patterns (no realistic false positives), and touches only the audit tool (no marathon-core contact, no byte-stability impact).

survivors.title: Frozen Windows .exe carries no version resource while the macOS .app embeds CFBundleVersion (file-metadata parity gap)
survivors.evidence: The shared spec reads `VERSION = _read_version()` and stamps it into the macOS bundle (`version=VERSION`, `"CFBundleShortVersionString": VERSION` at lines 195-209), but the Windows/Linux `EXE(...)` branch passes no `version=` argument — so the shipped YHWH.exe exposes no File Version / Product Version in Explorer's Details tab, unlike the .app. The Inno installer sets AppVersion, but the bundled binary itself stays version-less on Windows.

survivors.verifierFix:
The finder's approach is correct (generate a PyInstaller VSVersionInfo and pass version= in the EXE branch), with one required refinement so the build doesn't crash and one simplification:

1) Windows VS_VERSION_INFO filevers/prodvers MUST be a 4-tuple of ints. VERSION is '0.1.0' (3-part), so parse it: take the first VERSION line, split on '.', pad to 4, cast to int -> (0,1,0,0). Use the raw string for the StringFileInfo FileVersion/ProductVersion entries.

2) Build the VSVersionInfo in-spec (no separate file to maintain) and pass it to EXE(version=...). Example sketch to add before the else-branch EXE():
   from PyInstaller.utils.win32.versioninfo import (VSVersionInfo, FixedFileInfo, StringFileInfo, StringTable, StringStruct, VarFileInfo, VarStruct)
   _v = [int(p) for p in (VERSION.split('.') + ['0','0','0','0'])[:4]]
   _verinfo = VSVersionInfo(ffi=FixedFileInfo(filevers=tuple(_v), prodvers=tuple(_v)),
       kids=[StringFileInfo([StringTable('040904B0', [StringStruct('CompanyName','YHWH Ya\' Way'), StringStruct('FileDescription','YHWH Ya\' Way'), StringStruct('FileVersion', VERSION), StringStruct('ProductName','YHWH'), StringStruct('ProductVersion', VERSION), StringStruct('LegalCopyright','Source-available; incorporates public-domain texts.')])]), VarFileInfo([VarStruct('Translation', [1033, 1200])])])
   then add  version=_verinfo  to the else-branch EXE(...).

3) PyInstaller ignores version= on Linux (same as icon=), so no sys.platform guard is strictly needed, but importing the win32 helper at module top would fail on a macOS/Linux host. So guard the import+VSVersionInfo construction with `if sys.platform == 'win32'` and pass `version=_verinfo if sys.platform == 'win32' else None`. This keeps the spec cross-platform and additive; it touches only the launcher binary metadata, not the marathon core and not the KJV EPUB output.
